blocks.es_reference: 📖 Teología Sistemática — Unidad 12: Juicio, Cielo y el Reino de Dios

blocks.en: Professor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers
blocks.es_reference: Profesor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers

blocks.en: "We must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ." — 2 Corinthians 5:10 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "Es necesario que todos nosotros comparezcamos ante el tribunal de Cristo." — 2 Corintios 5:10 (RVG)

blocks.en: "The kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of our Lord and of his Messiah, and he will reign for ever and ever." — Revelation 11:15
blocks.es_reference: "Los reinos del mundo han venido a ser de nuestro Señor y de su Cristo; y él reinará por los siglos de los siglos." — Apocalipsis 11:15

blocks.en: The Reality of Judgment
blocks.es_reference: La Realidad del Juicio

blocks.en: Every person who has ever lived is moving toward a fixed and unavoidable appointment. The writer of Hebrews states it with unmistakable clarity: "It is appointed unto man once to die, and after that the judgment" (Hebrews 9:27). This is not a possibility or a remote contingency. It is certain. Every life will stand before God. Nothing is hidden. Ecclesiastes 12:14 declares, "For God will bring every work into judgment, including every secret thing, whether good or evil."
blocks.es_reference: Cada persona que ha vivido se mueve hacia una cita fija e inevitable. El escritor de Hebreos lo declara con claridad inconfundible: "Está establecido para los hombres que mueran una sola vez, y después de esto el juicio" (Hebreos 9:27). Esto no es una posibilidad o una contingencia remota. Es cierto. Cada vida se presentará ante Dios. Nada está oculto. Eclesiastés 12:14 declara: "Porque Dios traerá toda obra a juicio, juntamente con toda cosa encubierta, sea buena o sea mala".

blocks.en: For the unbeliever, judgment is based on works alone. There is no mediator, no advocate, no one to plead their case. Their own righteousness — or more accurately, their lack of it — is the standard by which they are measured. Paul writes in Romans 1:20 that they are "without excuse." The evidence of God in creation is sufficient to leave humanity accountable. Those who have rejected God's self-disclosure will be judged according to what they have done with the knowledge they received.
blocks.es_reference: Para el incrédulo, el juicio se basa solo en las obras. No hay mediador, ni abogado, ni nadie que defienda su caso. Su propia justicia — o más exactamente, su falta de ella — es el estándar por el cual son medidos. Pablo escribe en Romanos 1:20 que ellos están "sin excusa". La evidencia de Dios en la creación es suficiente para dejar a la humanidad responsable. Aquellos que han rechazado la auto-revelación de Dios serán juzgados según lo que han hecho con el conocimiento que recibieron.

blocks.en: For the believer, however, there is a different reality altogether. "There is therefore now no condemnation to those who are in Christ Jesus" (Romans 8:1). The condemnation that sin deserves has already been borne by Christ on the cross. The believer will not face judgment for sin, because the penalty has been fully paid. The case is closed. The debt is satisfied. Yet believers are still evaluated. Paul writes, "We must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ, that each one may receive the things done in the body, according to what he has done, whether good or bad" (2 Corinthians 5:10). This is not a judgment for sin — that has been settled at the cross. This is an evaluation for reward. It is the difference between a criminal trial, where guilt or innocence is determined, and an awards ceremony, where faithfulness is recognized.
blocks.es_reference: Para el creyente, sin embargo, hay una realidad completamente diferente. "Ahora, pues, ninguna condenación hay para los que están en Cristo Jesús" (Romanos 8:1). La condenación que el pecado merece ya ha sido llevada por Cristo en la cruz. El creyente no enfrentará juicio por el pecado, porque la pena ha sido plenamente pagada. El caso está cerrado. La deuda está satisfecha. Sin embargo, los creyentes todavía son evaluados. Pablo escribe: "Porque es necesario que todos nosotros comparezcamos ante el tribunal de Cristo, para que cada uno reciba según lo que haya hecho mientras estaba en el cuerpo, sea bueno o sea malo" (2 Corintios 5:10). Esto no es un juicio por el pecado — eso fue resuelto en la cruz. Esta es una evaluación para recompensa. Es la diferencia entre un juicio criminal, donde se determina la culpabilidad o inocencia, y una ceremonia de premiación, donde se reconoce la fidelidad.

blocks.en: The Reality of Hell
blocks.es_reference: La Realidad del Infierno

blocks.en: Few subjects are more avoided in modern preaching than hell. It is uncomfortable. It is unpopular. It seems harsh to the modern mind. Yet despite this cultural aversion, Jesus spoke more about hell than anyone else in Scripture. He did not shy away from warning people about the reality of eternal judgment. He said, "Fear Him who is able to destroy both soul and body in hell" (Matthew 10:28).
blocks.es_reference: Pocos temas se evitan más en la predicación moderna que el infierno. Es incómodo. Es impopular. Parece duro para la mente moderna. Sin embargo, a pesar de esta aversión cultural, Jesús habló más sobre el infierno que cualquier otro en la Escritura. No rehuyó advertir a la gente sobre la realidad del juicio eterno. Dijo: "Temed más bien a aquel que puede destruir el alma y el cuerpo en el infierno" (Mateo 10:28).

blocks.en: Hell is not an invention of the medieval church. It is not a scare tactic designed to manipulate people into religious compliance. It is the solemn teaching of Jesus Christ Himself. He described it as a place of "weeping and gnashing of teeth" (Matthew 8:12). He spoke of it as a fire that is not quenched (Mark 9:48). He called it "outer darkness" (Matthew 25:30). He described it as a place of conscious, unending suffering.
blocks.es_reference: El infierno no es una invención de la iglesia medieval. No es una táctica de miedo diseñada para manipular a las personas hacia el cumplimiento religioso. Es la enseñanza solemne de Jesucristo mismo. Lo describió como un lugar de "llanto y crujir de dientes" (Mateo 8:12). Habló de él como un fuego que no se apaga (Marcos 9:48). Lo llamó "las tinieblas de afuera" (Mateo 25:30). Lo describió como un lugar de sufrimiento consciente e interminable.

blocks.en: Hell is punishment. It is not rehabilitation. It is not purgatory. It is not a second chance. It is the just and holy response of a righteous God to unrepentant sin. The Apostle Paul declares, "These shall be punished with everlasting destruction from the presence of the Lord" (2 Thessalonians 1:9). The essence of hell is separation — separation from God, from His goodness, from His grace, from everything that makes life meaningful. Paul also states plainly, "The wages of sin is death" (Romans 6:23).
blocks.es_reference: El infierno es castigo. No es rehabilitación. No es purgatorio. No es una segunda oportunidad. Es la respuesta justa y santa de un Dios justo al pecado no arrepentido. El apóstol Pablo declara: "Los cuales sufrirán pena de eterna perdición, excluidos de la presencia del Señor" (2 Tesalonicenses 1:9). La esencia del infierno es la separación — separación de Dios, de Su bondad, de Su gracia, de todo lo que hace la vida significativa. Pablo también declara claramente: "La paga del pecado es muerte" (Romanos 6:23).

blocks.en: The doctrine of hell is difficult. No one should speak of it with glee or satisfaction. But neither should it be silenced out of fear or embarrassment. Jesus spoke of hell because He loved people and wanted to warn them. To remove the doctrine of hell from Christian teaching is to remove the very reason for the urgency of evangelism.
blocks.es_reference: La doctrina del infierno es difícil. Nadie debería hablar de ella con regocijo o satisfacción. Pero tampoco debería silenciarse por miedo o vergüenza. Jesús habló del infierno porque amaba a las personas y quería advertirles. Quitar la doctrina del infierno de la enseñanza cristiana es quitar la razón misma de la urgencia del evangelismo.

blocks.en: The Reality of Heaven
blocks.es_reference: La Realidad del Cielo

blocks.en: If hell is the bad news, heaven is the good news. The same Jesus who warned about hell also promised a place of eternal blessing for His followers. "I go to prepare a place for you" (John 14:2). Heaven is not a vague, disembodied state of floating on clouds. It is not an endless church service of boredom. It is a real place. It is the dwelling place of God. It is the final home of all who have trusted in Christ.
blocks.es_reference: Si el infierno es la mala noticia, el cielo es la buena noticia. El mismo Jesús que advirtió sobre el infierno también prometió un lugar de bendición eterna para Sus seguidores. "Voy, pues, a preparar lugar para vosotros" (Juan 14:2). El cielo no es un estado vago y desencarnado de flotar en las nubes. No es un servicio eclesiástico interminable de aburrimiento. Es un lugar real. Es la morada de Dios. Es el hogar final de todos los que han confiado en Cristo.

blocks.en: The Apostle John gives us a glimpse of heaven in Revelation 21. He describes the New Jerusalem as a city of unimaginable beauty — "having the glory of God" (Revelation 21:11). These images are symbolic, but they point to a reality that exceeds our capacity to fully comprehend. Paul echoes this same sense of surpassing glory when he writes that no eye has seen, no ear has heard, no mind has conceived what God has prepared for those who love Him (1 Corinthians 2:9) — words originally spoken of the wisdom God has now revealed to us by His Spirit, but fitting all the more for the fullness still to come.
blocks.es_reference: El apóstol Juan nos da un vislumbre del cielo en Apocalipsis 21. Describe la Nueva Jerusalén como una ciudad de belleza inimaginable — "teniendo la gloria de Dios" (Apocalipsis 21:11). Estas imágenes son simbólicas, pero apuntan a una realidad que excede nuestra capacidad de comprender plenamente. Pablo expresa este mismo sentido de gloria incomparable cuando escribe que ningún ojo ha visto, ningún oído ha oído, ninguna mente ha concebido lo que Dios ha preparado para los que le aman (1 Corintios 2:9) — palabras dichas originalmente sobre la sabiduría que Dios ya nos ha revelado por Su Espíritu, pero que encajan aún más con la plenitud que todavía está por venir.

blocks.en: One of the most significant aspects of heaven is that we will have new bodies. Paul writes that our earthly bodies, which are subject to weakness, decay, and death, will be "conformed to His glorious body" (Philippians 3:21). John adds, "We shall be like Him" (1 John 3:2). The resurrection body of Jesus after His resurrection is the pattern for our glorified bodies. He could eat fish by the seashore (Luke 24:42-43), yet He could appear behind locked doors (John 20:19). He was recognizable, yet at times appeared different — as with the disciples on the road to Emmaus (Luke 24:16).
blocks.es_reference: Uno de los aspectos más significativos del cielo es que tendremos cuerpos nuevos. Pablo escribe que nuestros cuerpos terrenales, que están sujetos a debilidad, decadencia y muerte, serán "transformados a la semejanza de su cuerpo glorioso" (Filipenses 3:21). Juan añade: "Seremos semejantes a él" (1 Juan 3:2). El cuerpo de resurrección de Jesús después de Su resurrección es el patrón para nuestros cuerpos glorificados. Podía comer pescado a la orilla del mar (Lucas 24:42-43), sin embargo podía aparecer detrás de puertas cerradas (Juan 20:19). Era reconocible, sin embargo a veces aparecía diferente — como con los discípulos en el camino a Emaús (Lucas 24:16).

blocks.en: Heaven’s Greatest Blessing: God Himself
blocks.es_reference: La Mayor Bendición del Cielo: Dios Mismo

blocks.en: But the greatest blessing of heaven is not its beauty or its comfort. The greatest blessing is the presence of God Himself. John writes, "He will dwell with them, and they will be His people, and God Himself will be with them and be their God" (Revelation 21:3). Heaven is heaven because God is there. "He will wipe every tear from their eyes. There will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain, for the old order of things has passed away" (Revelation 21:4).
blocks.es_reference: Pero la mayor bendición del cielo no es su belleza o su comodidad. La mayor bendición es la presencia de Dios mismo. Juan escribe: "He aquí el tabernáculo de Dios con los hombres, y él morará con ellos; y ellos serán su pueblo, y Dios mismo estará con ellos como su Dios" (Apocalipsis 21:3). El cielo es el cielo porque Dios está allí. "Enjugará Dios toda lágrima de los ojos de ellos; y ya no habrá muerte, ni habrá más llanto, ni clamor, ni dolor; porque las primeras cosas pasaron" (Apocalipsis 21:4).

blocks.en: The Intermediate State: Where Are We Now?
blocks.es_reference: El Estado Intermedio: ¿Dónde Estamos Ahora?

blocks.en: What happens to believers immediately after death, before the final resurrection? This is called the intermediate state. Scripture indicates that for the believer, to be absent from the body is to be present with the Lord (2 Corinthians 5:8). The Apostle Paul was torn between remaining in the body for the sake of ministry and departing to be with Christ, which he said was "far better" (Philippians 1:23). This suggests a conscious, joyful existence in the presence of Christ. The intermediate state is not the final state — we still await the resurrection of the body and the renewal of all things. But it is a state of peace, rest, and fellowship with the Lord. For the unbeliever, the intermediate state is described as a place of conscious suffering (Luke 16:19-31). The doctrine of the intermediate state gives believers confidence that death is not an end but a transition into the presence of Christ, where we will await the glorious resurrection at His return.
blocks.es_reference: ¿Qué sucede con los creyentes inmediatamente después de la muerte, antes de la resurrección final? Esto se llama el estado intermedio. La Escritura indica que para el creyente, estar ausente del cuerpo es estar presente con el Señor (2 Corintios 5:8). El apóstol Pablo estaba dividido entre permanecer en el cuerpo por el bien del ministerio y partir para estar con Cristo, lo cual dijo era "muchísimo mejor" (Filipenses 1:23). Esto sugiere una existencia consciente y gozosa en la presencia de Cristo. El estado intermedio no es el estado final — todavía esperamos la resurrección del cuerpo y la renovación de todas las cosas. Pero es un estado de paz, descanso y comunión con el Señor. Para el incrédulo, el estado intermedio se describe como un lugar de sufrimiento consciente (Lucas 16:19-31). La doctrina del estado intermedio da a los creyentes la confianza de que la muerte no es un fin sino una transición a la presencia de Cristo, donde esperaremos la gloriosa resurrección en Su regreso.

blocks.en: The Kingdom of God
blocks.es_reference: El Reino de Dios

blocks.en: During the time of the judges, before Israel had a human king, the final verse of the book summarizes the spiritual condition of the nation: "Everyone did what was right in his own eyes" (Judges 21:25). There was no recognized authority. There was no acknowledged King. Every person became a law unto themselves. The result was chaos, corruption, and suffering.
blocks.es_reference: Durante el tiempo de los jueces, antes que Israel tuviera un rey humano, el versículo final del libro resume la condición espiritual de la nación: "Cada uno hacía lo que bien le parecía" (Jueces 21:25). No había autoridad reconocida. No había Rey reconocido. Cada persona se convirtió en ley para sí misma. El resultado fue el caos, la corrupción y el sufrimiento.

blocks.en: The Kingdom of God is the answer to that chaos. God alone is King. He does not share His throne with any other. The Old Testament promises are clear: "Your throne shall be established forever" (2 Samuel 7:16). Daniel declares, "His dominion is an everlasting dominion, and His kingdom endures from generation to generation" (Daniel 4:34). The Kingdom of God is not a physical territory with borders, but the sovereignty, rule, and reign of God over all creation. As William Barclay notes, the Kingdom exists wherever God's will is perfectly obeyed. It is the condition wherein human hearts and actions align with the Creator's intent.
blocks.es_reference: El Reino de Dios es la respuesta a ese caos. Solo Dios es Rey. Él no comparte Su trono con ningún otro. Las promesas del Antiguo Testamento son claras: "Tu trono será estable eternamente" (2 Samuel 7:16). Daniel declara: "Su dominio es dominio eterno, y su reino por todas las edades" (Daniel 4:34). El Reino de Dios no es un territorio físico con fronteras, sino la soberanía, el gobierno y el reinado de Dios sobre toda la creación. Como William Barclay nota, el Reino existe dondequiera que la voluntad de Dios sea perfectamente obedecida. Es la condición en la que los corazones humanos y las acciones se alinean con la intención del Creador.

blocks.en: The Kingdom Fulfilled
blocks.es_reference: El Reino Consumado

blocks.en: Despite the chaos of the present age, the Kingdom of God is moving toward a fixed and certain conclusion. History is not random. It is not meaningless. It is not spiraling into nothingness. History is the unfolding of God's purposes, and those purposes will culminate in the visible, eternal reign of Christ.
blocks.es_reference: A pesar del caos de la edad presente, el Reino de Dios se mueve hacia una conclusión fija y cierta. La historia no es aleatoria. No es sin sentido. No está dando vueltas hacia la nada. La historia es el desarrollo de los propósitos de Dios, y esos propósitos culminarán en el reinado visible y eterno de Cristo.

blocks.en: Jesus taught that the Kingdom is both present and future. He said, "The Kingdom of God is among you" (Luke 17:21), indicating its present spiritual reality. Yet He also taught His disciples to pray, "Your Kingdom come" (Matthew 6:10), looking forward to its future, physical manifestation. The Kingdom is where God's will is done perfectly and completely.
blocks.es_reference: Jesús enseñó que el Reino es tanto presente como futuro. Dijo: "El reino de Dios está entre vosotros" (Lucas 17:21), indicando su realidad espiritual presente. Sin embargo, también enseñó a Sus discípulos a orar: "Venga tu reino" (Mateo 6:10), mirando hacia su manifestación física y futura. El Reino es donde la voluntad de Dios se hace perfecta y completamente.

blocks.en: The fulfillment of the Kingdom will come when Christ returns. Revelation 11:15 announces the final victory: "The kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of our Lord and of his Messiah, and he will reign for ever and ever." At that moment, every knee will bow and every tongue will confess that Jesus Christ is Lord (Philippians 2:10-11). The rebellion will end. The enemies will be vanquished. The King will take His throne.
blocks.es_reference: El cumplimiento del Reino vendrá cuando Cristo regrese. Apocalipsis 11:15 anuncia la victoria final: "Los reinos del mundo han venido a ser de nuestro Señor y de su Cristo; y él reinará por los siglos de los siglos". En ese momento, toda rodilla se doblará y toda lengua confesará que Jesucristo es Señor (Filipenses 2:10-11). La rebelión terminará. Los enemigos serán vencidos. El Rey tomará Su trono.

blocks.en: The final state is the new heaven and the new earth, where God dwells with His people, and every tear is wiped away. There will be no more curse. The throne of God and of the Lamb will be in it, and His servants will serve Him. They will see His face (Revelation 22:3-4). This is the consummation — the end toward which all of history has been moving.
blocks.es_reference: El estado final es el nuevo cielo y la nueva tierra, donde Dios mora con Su pueblo, y toda lágrima es enjugada. No habrá más maldición. El trono de Dios y del Cordero estará en ella, y Sus siervos le servirán. Verán Su rostro (Apocalipsis 22:3-4). Esta es la consumación — el fin hacia el cual toda la historia se ha estado moviendo.

blocks.en: Final Word
blocks.es_reference: Palabra Final

blocks.en: "Shall not the Judge of all the earth do right?" — Genesis 18:25
blocks.es_reference: "El Juez de toda la tierra, ¿no ha de hacer lo que es justo?" — Génesis 18:25

blocks.en: We do not presume outcomes. We do not speculate on who is saved and who is not. That judgment belongs to God alone. He is just. He is righteous. He will do what is right, even when we cannot understand His ways. Our task is not to judge the world, but to proclaim the gospel. Our task is not to determine who is worthy, but to invite all to come.
blocks.es_reference: No presumimos resultados. No especulamos sobre quién es salvo y quién no. Ese juicio pertenece solo a Dios. Él es justo. Él es recto. Hará lo que es correcto, aun cuando no podamos entender Sus caminos. Nuestra tarea no es juzgar al mundo, sino proclamar el evangelio. Nuestra tarea no es determinar quién es digno, sino invitar a todos a venir.

blocks.en: "The Lord shall reign forever" — Exodus 15:18
blocks.es_reference: "Jehová reinará eternamente y para siempre." — Éxodo 15:18

blocks.en: This is the final truth. Whatever happens in the interim — whatever wars rage, whatever empires rise and fall, whatever suffering we endure — this remains certain: God reigns. His Kingdom will come. His will will be done. And those who trust in Christ will dwell in His presence forever. Maranatha — Come, Lord Jesus.
blocks.es_reference: Esta es la verdad final. Cualquier cosa que suceda en el ínterin — cualesquiera guerras que se desaten, cualesquiera imperios que se levanten y caigan, cualquier sufrimiento que soportemos — esto permanece cierto: Dios reina. Su Reino vendrá. Su voluntad se hará. Y aquellos que confían en Cristo morarán en Su presencia para siempre. Maranata — Ven, Señor Jesús.

sa.prompt: Explain the difference between the judgment of unbelievers and the evaluation of believers at the judgment seat of Christ.
sa.model: The unit distinguishes two different judgments. The judgment seat of Christ, described in 2 Corinthians 5:10, is where believers appear so that each may receive according to what he has done in the body. This is not a trial to decide their eternal destiny, which is already secure in Christ, but an evaluation of the believer's life and works for reward. The judgment of unbelievers is different in kind: it is a judgment of condemnation, determining the eternal consequence of those who are not in Christ. So the difference lies in purpose and outcome. For the believer it is an assessment leading to reward and loss of reward, conducted within salvation; for the unbeliever it is a judgment of guilt. The same God judges both, but the believer faces evaluation as one already accepted, while the unbeliever faces condemnation.

sa.prompt: Why did Jesus speak more about hell than anyone else in Scripture? What does this reveal about His character?
sa.model: The unit notes that Jesus spoke about hell more than anyone else in Scripture and did not shy away from warning people about eternal judgment, even telling them to fear the One able to destroy both soul and body. Far from contradicting His love, this reveals His character. A truly loving person warns others of real danger rather than staying silent to spare discomfort. Jesus' frequent and sober warnings about hell flow from compassion: He took the reality of judgment seriously precisely because He cared about where people would spend eternity. His willingness to speak the hard truth shows that genuine love does not flatter or minimize danger but tells the truth in order to save. So the One who spoke most about hell is also the One who came to rescue people from it, and His warnings are an expression of love, not its absence.

sa.prompt: What does the Bible teach about glorified bodies, and how do they differ from our current bodies?
sa.model: The unit teaches about glorified bodies by pointing to the risen Christ as the pattern. His resurrection body was real and physical: He could eat fish by the seashore, and He was recognizable as Himself. Yet it also had new capacities, since He could appear behind locked doors and at times appeared different. So the glorified body is continuous with our present body, truly bodily and personal, not a ghost, but it is also transformed and freed from present limitations. The difference is that our current bodies are subject to weakness, decay, and death, while the glorified body is raised imperishable and fitted for eternal life in God's presence. The resurrection of Jesus shows that believers will not be disembodied spirits but will have real, recognizable bodies, redeemed and glorified, no longer bound by the frailty that marks us now.

sa.prompt: Explain the concept of the Kingdom of God. Is it present, future, or both? Support your answer.
sa.model: The unit presents the Kingdom of God as God's reign, and teaches that it is both present and future. It is present now in that God truly reigns and His kingdom is at work in the lives of His people; the rule of God has already broken into the world. Yet it is also future, awaiting its full consummation when God's reign is openly and completely established. The unit contrasts the kingdom with the era of the judges, when there was no king and everyone did what was right in his own eyes, to highlight the blessing of being under God's rule. So the right answer is both: believers already live under God's reign while still looking forward to its fulfillment. This is the same already-and-not-yet pattern, and it means the kingdom is a present reality to be lived in now and a future hope to be awaited.

sa.prompt: What is the significance of the phrase "Maranatha," and how should it shape the Christian's daily life?
sa.model: The unit explains Maranatha as the prayer and cry, Come, Lord Jesus. It expresses the longing of the church for the return of Christ, a heartfelt plea that the Lord would come and bring His purposes to completion. Its significance is that it captures the expectant, hope-filled posture that should mark believers as they await the consummation of all things. This should shape daily life by keeping the Christian oriented toward Christ's return rather than absorbed only in the present. Living in a Maranatha spirit means holding earthly things loosely, longing for the Lord, and living each day ready and watchful. It turns the hope of Christ's coming into a daily attitude of expectation that steadies believers in suffering and motivates faithful, holy living, since the One for whom they pray may come at any time.

sa.prompt: What does Revelation 21:1-4 teach about the final state? What will be absent, and what will be present?
sa.model: The unit draws on Revelation 21:1-4 to describe the final state as a new heaven and new earth, with the New Jerusalem pictured as a city of unimaginable beauty having the glory of God. The passage describes both what will be absent and what will be present. Absent will be the things that mark this fallen world: death, mourning, crying, and pain, all of which pass away. Present will be the dwelling of God with His people, as God Himself wipes away every tear and lives among them. The unit treats the imagery as symbolic yet pointing to a glorious reality. The greatest feature of the final state is not the beauty of the place but the presence of God with His people. So the final state is the removal of all that sin brought and the restoration of unbroken fellowship with God in a renewed creation.

sa.prompt: How does the doctrine of final judgment produce hope and motivate holiness in believers?
sa.model: The unit teaches that the doctrine of final judgment is not only sobering but also produces hope and motivates holiness. It produces hope because it assures believers that God will set all things right: evil will not go unanswered, justice will finally be done, and the wrongs of this world will be addressed by a righteous Judge. For those in Christ, the prospect of standing before Him is not terror but the hope of receiving reward for a faithful life. At the same time, knowing we are accountable and will give an account of what we have done motivates holiness now. Because our lives will be evaluated, we are moved to live carefully and faithfully rather than carelessly. So final judgment functions in two directions for the believer: it comforts with the promise of justice and reward, and it spurs godly living by reminding us that how we live matters to God.

sa.prompt: What does it mean that "the Lord shall reign forever" (Exodus 15:18), and how does this provide comfort in suffering?
sa.model: The unit presents the declaration that the Lord shall reign forever, from Exodus 15:18, as the final and steadying truth of the whole course. It means that God's reign is not temporary or threatened; whatever happens in the meantime, He remains on the throne and His rule has no end. This provides comfort in suffering because it sets present troubles within a larger certainty. Wars may rage, empires may rise and fall, and believers may endure real pain, but none of these can overturn God's everlasting reign. The sufferer can take heart that the powers causing the trouble are passing, while God's kingdom is permanent and will have the last word. So the eternal reign of the Lord anchors hope: the believer's confidence rests not on present circumstances but on the unshakable, never-ending sovereignty of God, who will bring His purposes to a triumphant end.

sa.prompt: Explain the significance of the intermediate state. Where are believers immediately after death?
sa.model: The unit explains the intermediate state as the believer's condition between death and the future resurrection of the body. Scripture indicates that for the believer, to be absent from the body is to be present with the Lord, as Paul says in 2 Corinthians 5:8. So immediately after death the believer is consciously with Christ, not annihilated and not asleep in nothingness, but in the Lord's presence. The unit notes that Paul was torn between staying to serve and departing to be with Christ, which he regarded as far better. The intermediate state is significant because it assures believers that death does not separate them from their Lord; the moment they leave the body they are with Him. Yet it is intermediate, not final, because the fullness of redemption still awaits the resurrection of the body and the renewed creation. Until then, the believing dead are present with Christ.

sa.prompt: Summarize the main point of Unit 12. How should judgment, hell, heaven, and the reign of God affect how we live today?
sa.model: The main point of the unit is that the certainty of judgment, the reality of hell, the hope of heaven, and the eternal reign of God are meant to shape how believers live today. Judgment reminds us we are accountable and moves us toward holiness while assuring us of justice and reward. The reality of hell, of which Jesus spoke so often out of love, makes the gospel urgent and warns us to take eternity seriously. The hope of heaven, where God dwells with His people and death and pain are no more, fills the believer with comfort and longing, expressed in the cry Maranatha. And the truth that the Lord shall reign forever anchors confidence in every trial. Together these doctrines call us to live ready, watchful, holy, and hopeful, holding earthly things loosely, taking God's warnings seriously, and resting in the certainty that God reigns and will bring all things to a glorious end.
